correctness.rationale: All roots have orders r satisfying r/gcd(r,d^n)=m. Primitive order-r roots above alpha form a single Gal(Q(zeta_r)/Q(alpha)) orbit of size phi(r)/phi(m); Gal(KQ(zeta_r)/K) acts freely, so its orbit count is exactly [K intersect Q(zeta_r):Q(alpha)]. Kronecker–Weber gives a finite conductor C for E=K intersect Q^cyc, and cyclotomic intersection Q(zeta_C) intersect Q(zeta_r)=Q(zeta_gcd(C,r)) caps prime exponents. Summing stabilized coordinate intervals yields an exact finite polynomial, with positive highest-degree coefficient [H:F] product b_p; Euler totient sums yield the cyclotomic product. Independent Galois-orbit enumeration matched all 160 small cases (m=1..5, cyclotomic M, d=2,3,4,6 and n=1,2). Infinite claim rests on Galois and conductor arguments, not finite tests.
